etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English accumylaten, from Latin accumulātus, perfect passive participle of accumulō (“amass, pile up”), formed from ad (“to, towards, at”) + cumulō (“heap”), from cumulus (“a heap”). First attested in the 1520's.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To heap up in a mass; to pile up; to collect or bring together (either literally or figuratively)
(intransitive) To gradually grow or increase in quantity or number.

quote.citation: 1770, Oliver Goldsmith, The Deserted Village, lines 17–18:
quote.text: Ill fares the land, to hastening ills a prey, / Where wealth accumulates, and men decay.

definitions.definition: (education, dated) To take a higher degree at the same time with a lower degree, or at a shorter interval than usual.
